component.name: AppsScope
component.summary: Install apps and see exactly what they can access

description.p: AppsScope is an app store for Linux that tells you what an app can actually do to your computer before you install it.

Many Flatpak apps ship with unrestricted access to every file you own. Existing software centres reduce this to a vague warning, if they mention it at all. AppsScope grades every app in plain language, shows what an install will really download, and lets you revoke permissions without leaving the store.

ul.li: Every app graded: sandboxed, limited access, or full access
A consent dialog before installing, listing what you are granting
Real download sizes, including runtimes you do not have yet
Revoke permissions in place, shared with Flatseal and the CLI
Flatpak and distro packages side by side, clearly labelled

description.p: First release: Flatpak and distro package management, permission grading, and install-time disclosure.
